title: E is for EFIS: How to master the glass cockpit in heavy weather | MSFS A-Z
description:
Imagine flying through a blinding thunderstorm at 30,000 feet. You have split seconds to make a critical decision. Would you rather look at a chaotic maze of 20 different spinning mechanical dials, or a clean, glowing screen that processes everything for you instantly? In IFR conditions, your instruments are your only lifeline.

Welcome back to Microsoft Flight Simulator A to Z! In this episode, we are stepping into the modern era with the letter E for EFIS (Electronic Flight Instrument System). A lot of casual simmers just stare at the pretty glass screens without actually utilizing their true power. But if you want to fly like a real-world airline captain and never lose control in "the soup" again, understanding this layout is absolutely non-negotiable.

In this video, we break down the digitized revolution of the glass cockpit. We'll unpack the immediate survival data on your Primary Flight Display (PFD), reveal the hidden trend vector trick that real pilots use to pull off butter-smooth landings, and show you exactly how to manipulate your Navigation Display (ND) modes to dodge heavy VATSim traffic, fix flight plan discontinuities, and execute flawless blind instrument landings.

In this video, you’ll discover:

-The Glass Cockpit Revolution: How EFIS consolidated the exhausting "six-pack" mental dance into pure visual clarity.
- The PFD Survival Guide: How to easily read your airspeed, altitude tapes, and artificial horizon without burning out.
- The 6-Second Secret Weapon: How to track and use the yellow trend vector arrow to catch deviations early and nail your pitches.
- ND Mode Mastery: When to toggle between MAP mode for weather/traffic avoidance and PLAN mode to clean up routing gaps.
- Zero-Visibility Confidence: How switching to ILS/Approach mode strips away the clutter to guide you straight to the centerline.

🕒 Chapters
00:00 - Intro
00:42 - The Revolution - Steam vs. Glass
01:18 - The anatomy - The Primary Flight Display (PFD)
01:49 - The secret landing weapon: trend vectors
02:15 - The anatomy - Navigating with the Navigation Display (ND)
02:50 - Navigation Display - MAP/ARC mode
03:06 - Navigation Display - PLAN mode
03:29 - Navigation Display - ILS/Approach mode

Transitioning from a casual gamer to an elite flight simmer means taking total control of your cockpit environment. Next time you load into MSFS, actively manage your display modes and anticipate your trend vectors. If this breakdown helped sharpen your situational awareness, hit that like button, subscribe for the rest of our aviation alphabet series, and let me know in the comments: do you prefer old-school steam gauges or pristine glass cockpits?
